Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for running the package lab with our product team yesterday. We made a lot of progress mapping features to our projected traffic patterns, but we need a concise recommendation we can take to procurement — specifically:

- A suggested tier and seat/throughput mix for months 1, 6, and 12 (traffic estimates attached).
- Which add-ons are mandatory for HIPAA-sensitive flows vs. optional for cost savings.
- One clean fallback we can sign up for if we exceed our committed burst.

Can you turn the lab notes into a short decision memo and call out any near-term discounts or transitional credits you can offer if we commit to a 12‑month Dedicated plan? Procurement is on the cc.

Appreciate a draft by EOD Friday if possible — we’re aiming to present to the procurement committee next Tuesday.

Best,

Hi Stella —

Thanks for the clear asks. I ran the lab notes back to the team and pulled together a short decision memo and two pricing sketches that map to months 1/6/12. High level (see attached PDF + pricing grid):

1) Recommended path (low friction): Start on Hosted API for M1 (to avoid infra setup), transition to Dedicated 3-month pilot at M3, then full Dedicated at M6. This reduces initial ramp risk but keeps a committed baseline for discounts.

2) Tier/throughput suggestion:
  - M1: Hosted - 100k gen tokens/mo + Embedding on-demand
  - M6: Dedicated - Small pool (2xA40 equiv) with burst to Medium pool for peak windows
  - M12: Dedicated - Medium pool + prefix caching enabled, optional quantized model for lower-cost background jobs

3) HIPAA add-ons: KMS integration and extended audit retention are mandatory for any PHI workflows. WAF and private VPC are optional unless you require air-gapped ops.

4) Fallback: We recommend a routing policy that falls back to a lower-cost, higher-latency model variant in a second region — we’ll supply automated failover rules in the rollout config.

Discounts/credits: Ben is looping in the recommended commercial concessions below — the short version is a limited-time onboarding credit and a graduated usage discount after the first 90 days if you commit to a 12-month Dedicated SKU.

I attached a two-page memo and our pricing grid. Ben/Jonas — can you confirm the discount ranges and any procurement terms we should flag?

Lauren
Director, Growth Solutions
Redwood Inference

Lauren and team —

Thanks for the summary, Lauren. Quick commercial confirmation and a couple of options procurement might prefer:

Option A (Commit-heavy, best unit economics):
- 12-month Dedicated commit (Medium pool at steady-state)
- 18% list discount on compute + onboarding credit equal to one month of committed spend
- SLA addendum and extended log retention included in second year

Option B (Staged commit, lower immediate exposure):
- 6-month Dedicated pilot (small pool) with optional auto-scale to Medium during defined peak windows
- 10% list discount, onboarding credit of 25% of first-month committed spend
- Right to renegotiate rates at month 9 based on actual usage profile

Other commercial notes:
- We can include a one-time professional services credit for migration (covers VPC setup and model pinning) if HealthLane signs within 30 days of the pilot close.
- If procurement needs a clean single-line PO (no multi-SKU complexity), we can issue an umbrella order and track entitlements via internal tagging.

Jonas — please attach the draft redline for procurement-friendly language (cap on overage rates, billing cadence, and SLA exceptions) and I’ll fold it into the pricing grid.

Ben
